126-016.r: Tasmania → island state of Australia (across Bass Strait), not Uganda. Correct: Sicily → Italy; Newfoundland → Canada; Durban → South Africa.

126-018.r: Iceland lies south of the Arctic Circle; the Arctic Circle passes through Finland, Norway and Sweden.

126-019.r: Sun City → North-West province of South Africa, between the Elands River and the Pilanesberg mountains.

126-020.r: Largest cities: Canada → Toronto; Greece → Athens; Nigeria → Lagos; Syria → Damascus (book notes Aleppo is now Syria's most populous).

126-021.r: Davos → Switzerland; Barcelona → Spain; Auckland → New Zealand; Kandy → Sri Lanka.

126-022.r: Kanto plain → Japan; a highly developed, urbanised and industrial plain.

126-023.r: Mexico → North American continent; third largest there after Canada and USA; USA to its north, Guatemala and Belize to its south.

126-024.r: Congo (DR Congo) → Africa, on the Equator; Africa's second largest country after Algeria. The Equator also crosses the Republic of Congo.

126-025.r: Malta → small island country of southern Europe in the Mediterranean Sea.

126-026.r: South to north: Jakarta (6°S) → Singapore (1.3°N) → Bangkok (13°N) → Hanoi (21°N).
126-026.h: Only Jakarta is south of the Equator, so it comes first; Singapore sits just north of it.

126-027.r: Aleppo → Syria; Mazar-i-Sharif → Afghanistan; Kirkuk and Mosul → Iraq (not Yemen or Palestine).

126-028.r: Ghazni and Kandahar → Afghanistan; Fergana and Samarkand → Uzbekistan, so they are not in Afghanistan.

126-029.r: Ground Zero → site of the World Trade Center Twin Towers, New York, destroyed in the 11 September 2001 attacks; complex now rebuilt.

127-001.r: Venice of the North → St. Petersburg (Russia, on the Neva River); title shared with Amsterdam, Bruges, Copenhagen, Hamburg, Manchester, Stockholm.

127-002.r: Midnight sun → north of the Arctic Circle and south of the Antarctic Circle, so at both North and South Poles; Norway = land of the midnight sun.

127-003.r: Continent of Birds → South America (about 3402 of the world's 11000 bird species).

127-004.r: Niagara Falls → New York State; land of thousand lakes → Finland; Eiffel Tower → Paris; Roof of the World → Pamir.

127-005.r: Dark Continent → Africa; Roof of the World → Pamir; Country of thousand lakes → Finland; Pearls Island → Bahrain.

127-007.r: Mistress of the Eastern Sea (also Pearl of the Indian Ocean) → Sri Lanka. Ninety East Ridge → Indian Ocean.

127-009.r: Paris of (South) America → Buenos Aires, capital and largest city of Argentina, known for its wide roads.

127-010.r: Blue Grass State → Kentucky (East South-Central USA).

127-011.r: Gateway to the West → Istanbul (Turkey), bounded by the Sea of Marmara, Bosporus Strait and Golden Horn.

127-012.r: Land of White Elephants → Thailand (the white elephant is holy there).

127-013.r: Land of the Rising Sun → Japan ('Nippon' means land of the rising sun).

127-014.r: Garden of Lakes / Land of a Thousand Lakes → Finland (more than one lakh lakes).

127-015.r: City of canals → Venice, also called 'Queen of the Adriatic'.

127-016.r: City of the Golden Gate → San Francisco (Golden Gate Bridge across San Francisco Bay).

127-017.r: Manchester of the East → Osaka (Kansai region, Japan); historically also called 'Nation's Kitchen'.

127-018.r: Pearl of Siberia → Lake Baikal, world's oldest and deepest freshwater lake.

127-019.r: Land of Morning Calm → Korea (South Korea).

127-020.r: Oil Capital of Europe → Aberdeen, which grew with North Sea oil.
127-020.c: The book dates the North Sea oil finds to the mid-nineteenth century; they were made in the second half of the twentieth century.

127-021.r: Land of Promise → Mindanao, an island of the Philippines.

128-001.r: OMT is measured to the 26°C isotherm, at 59 m (not 129 m) in SW Indian Ocean in Jan-Mar; Jan-Mar OMT helps predict monsoon rainfall vs long-term mean.

128-002.r: Water covers about 71% (70.9%) of Earth's surface, i.e. over two-thirds; land is about 29%.

128-003.r: Nearest sea-level point to Earth's centre → North Pole region (Arctic Ocean), about 6353 km from the centre.

128-004.r: Datum line → horizontal line at sea level from which all heights and depths are measured.

128-005.r: Largest part of the hydrosphere → Pacific Ocean; order by area: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.

128-006.r: Mid-Oceanic Ridge → about 64000-65000 km long, through Atlantic, Indian and Pacific oceans; single largest geological feature on Earth's surface.

128-007.r: Ninety East Ridge → Indian Ocean, along 90°E; about 5000 km long, from 34°S to 10°N.

128-008.r: Gravitational water fills large soil pores and drains down by gravity; its tension is zero or below 1/3 atmosphere.

128-009.r: Earth's water: 96.5% salt; 2.5% fresh, mostly in glaciers and polar ice (68.7%, not 95%); usable fresh water under 1%; next largest store is groundwater.

128-013.r: World water, descending: oceans (96.5%) > polar ice and glaciers (1.74%) > groundwater (1.7%) > rivers (0.0002%).

128-014.r: Most extensive ocean-floor zone → deep sea (abyssal) plains, 3000-6000 m deep, over 76% of ocean basin area.

128-015.r: Red Sea → example of an axial trough, between Africa and Arabia; a magnetic anomaly is found there.

128-016.r: Telegraph Plateau → Atlantic Ocean, not Indian. Correct: Cocoa Ridge → Pacific; Walvis Ridge → Atlantic; Agulhas Basin → Indian Ocean.

128-017.r: Indian Ocean → ancient Greeks' 'Erythraean Sea'; spreads on both sides of the Equator (about 30°N to 60°S).

129-001.r: Baku, capital of Azerbaijan → on the Caspian Sea coast; the Caspian is the largest saltwater lake.

129-002.r: Black Sea → north of Turkey. Turkey's seas: Black (north), Aegean (west), Marmara (north-west), Mediterranean (south).

129-003.r: Turkey (Turkiye) → between the Black Sea (north) and Mediterranean Sea (south); Aegean to the west, Sea of Marmara to the north-west.

129-004.r: Seas from west to east: Mediterranean → Black Sea → Caspian Sea → Aral Sea.
129-004.h: 'My Big Cat Ate': Mediterranean, Black, Caspian, Aral.

129-005.r: Inland sea → Caspian Sea, world's largest inland sea and largest lake (about 371000 sq km).

129-006.r: Sargasso Sea → North Atlantic Ocean, named after the sargassum seaweed found there.

129-007.r: Sargasso Sea → North Atlantic Ocean; the only sea without a land boundary.

129-008.r: Sargasso Sea → part of the North Atlantic; marked by typical marine vegetation (sargassum seaweed).

129-010.r: Sargasso Sea has no coastline: a mid-North Atlantic sea bounded only by currents (Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Canary, North Equatorial).

129-011.r: Tyrrhenian Sea → bounded by the Italian peninsula, Sicily, Sardinia and Corsica.

129-012.r: Aral Sea (Central Asian lake) → bordered by Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

129-013.r: Chad is landlocked, so no Mediterranean coast; Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt border the Mediterranean.

129-014.r: Jordan has no Mediterranean coast (Dead Sea to west, Red Sea to south-west; capital Amman); Syria, Lebanon, Israel open to it.

129-015.r: Gaza Strip → on the Mediterranean Sea, between Egypt and Israel; governed by Hamas since 2007.

129-016.r: Deepest of these seas → South China Sea (about 5560 m); Mediterranean 5267 m, Sea of Japan 3742 m, Bering Sea 3500 m.

129-017.r: Correct: Adriatic–Albania, Caspian–Kazakhstan, Mediterranean–Morocco. Wrong: Black Sea–Croatia, Red Sea–Syria (Red Sea: Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti).

129-018.r: Black Sea's six countries: Russia, Ukraine, Romania, Bulgaria, Turkiye, Georgia. Syria lies on the Mediterranean, not the Black Sea.

129-019.r: Red Sea → axial trough between Africa and Arabia, with magnetic anomalies; key trade link after the Suez Canal opened.

129-020.r: Mediterranean borders Lebanon and Syria, not Jordan or Iraq; joined to the Atlantic by Gibraltar Strait, to the Red Sea by Suez Canal.

129-021.r: Baltic Sea's 9 coastal countries: Denmark, Germany, Poland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Russia, Finland, Sweden. Norway is not one.

129-022.r: Red Sea: very little precipitation and no river inflow; opens to the Indian Ocean via Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden.

130-001.r: Ocean currents are driven by Earth's rotation, wind and air pressure, and density (temperature, salinity) differences; not by Earth's revolution.

130-002.r: Ocean currents: slow surface flows, set mainly by prevailing winds, help Earth's heat balance, shaped by ocean configuration; all four statements true.

130-003.r: North Indian Ocean currents reverse twice a year with NE and SW monsoon winds (monsoon drift); South Indian Ocean currents keep a fixed pattern.

130-004.r: Agulhas → warm (not cold) current of the South Indian Ocean; formed by Madagascar and Mozambique currents, later joins the West Wind Drift.

130-007.r: North Atlantic Drift carries warm Gulf Stream water to Europe; sub-polar Norway benefits most, as the warm water checks ice cover.

130-008.r: Benguela → only cold current of the South Atlantic; flows north along the west coast of southern Africa, joins South Equatorial current. Brazil current is warm.

130-009.r: Benguela → cold South Atlantic current (west coast of Africa), not Indian Ocean. Agulhas, Mozambique, South Indian Ocean currents → Indian Ocean.

130-010.r: Warm: Agulhas, Brazil currents. Cold: Humboldt (Peru), California currents.

130-011.r: South Atlantic circuit: South Equatorial → Brazil → West Wind Drift → Benguela; the Canary current is not part of it.

130-012.r: Benguela → cold current of the South Atlantic. Gulf Stream, Norwegian and Florida → warm currents of the North Atlantic.

130-013.r: Peruvian (Humboldt) → cold SE Pacific current off west South America; Benguela, Brazilian, South Equatorial → Atlantic circuit.

130-014.r: Ocean salinity peaks near the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn (low rain, high evaporation). Benguela is not Pacific; cold Humboldt (Peruvian) is not North Pacific.

130-017.r: Gulf Stream → powerful warm current of the North Atlantic; starts in the Gulf of Mexico as Florida current; found by Ponce de Leon in 1513.

130-018.r: Map pair → Benguela Current (cold, flowing south to north) and Guinea Current (flowing north to south).

130-019.r: Gulf Stream → warm current; West Wind Drift → slow eastward flow in westerly zone; Peru Current → Pacific; West Australian Current → Indian Ocean.

130-020.r: Equatorial counter-current flows west to east between North and South Equatorial currents, from water piling up where they converge. Canaries current → not Pacific.

130-022.r: Benguela → Atlantic (north along the south-west African coast). Humboldt (Peru), California and Alaska currents → Pacific.

130-023.r: Warm: Brazil, Gulf Stream, Kuroshio. Cold: Falkland, Labrador, Canary.

131-001.r: Halocline → zone where salinity changes rapidly with depth (the salinity gradient).

131-002.r: Main source of sea salinity → land (rivers carry its salts); average sea salinity is about 35‰.

131-003.r: Sodium chloride → largest share of sea salts (77.8%), then magnesium chloride (10.9%); Dittmar's 1884 Challenger report: 47 salts, 7 main.

131-004.r: Salinity per book: Lake Van (Turkey) 330‰ > Dead Sea 238‰ > Great Salt Lake 220‰ > Red Sea 36-41‰; when Van is absent, answer Dead Sea.
131-004.c: Lake Van's 330‰ is an old textbook figure that exam keys follow; measured salinity of Lake Van is far lower than the Dead Sea's.

131-008.r: Red Sea (36-41‰) is the saltiest true sea here; Mediterranean 37-39‰; Dead Sea and Caspian are lakes, though the Dead Sea is saltiest overall.
131-008.c: The book gives no single answer (*): Red Sea if only true seas count, Dead Sea if all options are taken as seas.

131-009.r: Higher sea-water density means higher salinity; no fixed law links salinity with depth, it varies with depth from place to place.
131-009.c: The book gives no single answer (*): density rises with salinity, but depth does not change in a fixed way.

131-010.r: Great Salt Lake → Utah, USA; salinity 220‰.

131-011.r: Arabian Sea salinity about 36‰ (nearest option 35 ppt); Bay of Bengal about 30‰; Indian Ocean at 0-10° latitude 35.14‰.

131-012.r: Highest average salinity among these seas → Dead Sea (238‰); world's highest → Lake Assal (348‰).

132-001.r: Tides → Moon's gravitational pull plus centripetal and centrifugal forces; the indirect high tide (side away from the Moon) → Earth's centrifugal force.

132-004.r: Neap tide → high tide below normal (about 20% less), low tide above normal; comes on 7th-8th day after new or full moon, not at new moon.

132-005.r: Highest tide (spring tide) → Sun, Earth and Moon in a straight line (syzygy) at full and new moon; perigean spring tide when the Moon is closest.

132-007.r: High tides are caused mainly by the Moon; its tide-producing power is 2.17 times the Sun's. Spring tide at full/new moon; neap tide on 7th-8th day.

133-001.r: Aleutian Trench → North Pacific; Kermadec → South Pacific; Sunda (Java) → Indian Ocean; South Sandwich → South Atlantic.

133-002.r: World's deepest trench → Mariana Trench (Pacific); its Challenger Deep, named after HMS Challenger, is the deepest point of the oceans.

133-004.r: Diamantina Trench (Diamantina Fracture Zone) → Indian Ocean, about 1125 km south-west of the Perth Basin.

133-005.r: Deepest points: Pacific → Mariana Trench; Atlantic → Puerto Rico Trench; Indian → Java (Sunda) Trench; Arctic → Eurasian Basin.

133-006.r: Sunda Trench → eastern Indian Ocean, a 3200 km arc running parallel to both Sumatra and Java; hence 'more than one of the above'.

133-007.r: Deepest points: Pacific → Mariana Trench; Arctic → Molloy Deep; Indian → Sunda Trench; Atlantic → Puerto Rico Trench.

134-001.r: Correct: Volga → Caspian Sea; Zambezi → Indian Ocean. Wrong: Thames → North Sea (not Irish Sea); Mekong → South China Sea (not Andaman Sea).

134-002.r: Largest river by drainage area and flow → Amazon (basin about 70 lakh sq km; about 6437 km long); longest → Nile (6695 km).
134-002.t: Don't confuse largest (Amazon, by basin and volume) with longest (Nile).

134-003.r: Second longest river → Amazon (after the Nile); the largest river, its basin covers Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Colombia and others.

134-004.r: Congo (Zaire) River → crosses the Equator twice.

134-005.r: Congo Basin (WWF) → six countries: Cameroon, Central African Republic, DR Congo, Republic of Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon.

134-006.r: Longest rivers: Nile 6695 km > Amazon 6437 km > Yangtze 6300 km; Amazon is longer than Amur, Congo and Lena.

134-007.r: Longest river of South America → Amazon (about 6437 km; ships sail about 1600 km up it). World's longest → Nile (6695 km).

134-008.r: Chad is outside the Nile basin. Nile basin: Burundi, Rwanda, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan, Tanzania, Kenya, Eritrea, Uganda, Egypt.

134-009.r: Blue Nile → rises from Lake Tana, Ethiopia; called the Abbay in its upper course.

134-010.r: Egypt = 'Gift of the Nile': Nile water and fertile land make it an oasis in the Sahara; A and R true, R explains A.

134-011.r: Salween → flows north to south in eastern Myanmar; rises on the Tibetan Plateau, 2815 km long, falls into the Andaman Sea.

134-012.r: Salween flows south; Amur flows north-east; Lena and Ob flow north.

134-013.r: Wrong: Mekong flows south-east (not south-west) to the South China Sea. Amur → north-east; Syr Darya → north-west (Aral Sea); Angara → north.

134-014.r: Longest river of Asia → Yangtze (6300 km, China, into East China Sea); Hwang Ho 5464 km, Brahmaputra 2900 km, Indus 2880 km.

134-015.r: Map basins: A → Parana (South America); B → Ganga-Brahmaputra; C → Zambezi (Africa); D → Indus.

134-016.r: Map rivers: A → Yukon (Alaska, NW Canada); B → Mackenzie (Canada, into Beaufort Sea); C → St. Lawrence; D → Orinoco.

134-017.r: Amu Darya and Syr Darya (Central Asia) → flow into the Aral Sea.

134-018.r: Into the Black Sea: Dnieper and Danube (Europe's second longest). Volga, Europe's longest, flows into the Caspian Sea.

134-020.r: Lena → Arctic Ocean; Amur → Pacific Ocean; Tigris → Persian Gulf; Mahi → Arabian Sea.

134-021.r: Rhine → flows through a rift valley; rises in the Swiss Alps, enters the North Sea; Bonn lies on it.

134-022.r: Elbe and Rhine → both drain into the North Sea; Elbe basin about 1.5 lakh km².

134-023.r: Niger → Africa (Fouta Djallon Highlands to Gulf of Guinea), not Asia. Lop Nor (saline lake, China), Amur, Tigris → Asia.

134-024.r: Limpopo (Africa) → crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice.

134-025.r: Best radial drainage → Sri Lanka: rivers rise in the central highlands (about 1500 m) and flow outward to the sea.

134-026.r: Mahaweli Ganga → Sri Lanka's longest river (335 km), from the Hatton plateau to the Bay of Bengal.

134-027.r: Wrong: Rhone is not Spain's; it flows past Geneva (Switzerland) into the Bay of Lions, Mediterranean. Correct: Dnieper–Ukraine, Po–Italy, Rhine–Germany.

134-028.r: Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam to the South China Sea; not through Malaysia or Bangladesh.

134-030.r: Lake Itasca (glacial lake) → source of the Mississippi, which flows into the Gulf of Mexico; Ohio, Arkansas, Red River are tributaries.

134-031.r: Mekong rises on the Tibetan Plateau, flows 4909 km to the South China Sea; its delta is in southern Vietnam (and Cambodia), not southern Cambodia.

134-032.r: Bird's foot delta → mouth of the Mississippi River.

134-033.r: Grand Canyon (Arizona, USA) → cut by the Colorado River, mainly in the last 5-6 million years.
